jobs.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Production title-screen environmental key art for Joseon Hunters, a 3D isometric dark Korean fantasy action RPG. Match a grounded, hand-painted matte 3D game environment, with legible medium-sized silhouettes, restrained texture frequency, rough dark timber and worn slate/granite, warm practical light only. Korean village vernacular (Joseon-inspired fictional Korea), NOT Chinese palaces, NOT Japanese architecture, NOT European medieval. No people, no beasts, no text, no lettering, no logo, no menus, no UI. Landscape widescreen 16:9. Same composition for both candidates: camera at a fixed elevated three-quarter angle approximately 30 degrees looking down along a walkable path leading from lower center to upper-right focal area. Left 36 percent and upper-left must be quiet very dark charcoal shadow as negative space for the logo and four large menu buttons. The right half has the rich environmental focal point. The path must clearly read as traversable. Desaturated charcoal, muted earth, faded navy, faint warm amber lights. Restrained and dangerous, sparse ominous details, no amusement-park haunted house, no neon magic glow, no white snowy setting, no decorative border. The overall image must look like high-quality lighting of a real playable ARPG location, with broad forms and natural indirect light, not a flat bright anime poster. No heavy bloom. Readable, not crushed black. All flames small and localized so they can be animated as practical lights in the game title screen. Preserve the calm left menu region. Subject: the village of Motgol at late blue dusk, a wider compact Korean settlement of low crooked wooden houses, weathered thatched roofs, one tiled-roof modest tavern, wooden gate posts, stacked clay jars, a stone-lined dirt road, loose ropes and a neglected talisman paper at one doorway. The focal point is the tavern and distant village gate on the right third. Two subtle small lantern flames (one tavern eave, one road post) and low ground-hugging fog tucked behind wooden posts. The path and roof arrangement suggest a lived-in refuge at the edge of danger. Korean dark fantasy, dark slate sky, no sunset spectacle. No supernatural characters. Make the architecture distinctively Korean and modest.
